newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bund futures holding earlier gains in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Bund futures holding earlier gains in late trade.

text.p: Bund futures were solidly higher in late trade, maintaining gains posted in the morning linked to firm Treasuries and a technical correction to losses last week.
Traders said that although Bunds are well bid, they should closely track Treasuries with the direction of U.S. interest rates more open to question than in Germany.
The June DTB Bund futures contract was up 31 basis points in late trade at 101.77. It had traded in a range between 101.58 and 101.81.

The yield curve flattened sharply on the day, narrowing six basis points to 203 basis points with the long-end of the curve outperforming. "We expect to see this flattening trend continue in the coming months, with our sights set on a test of 175 basis points in the next 2-3 months and down to 150 basis points byond that in three months," wrote Bear Stearns in a market commentary published today.

Speculation about a delay in the launch of monetary union, meanwhile, gathered momentum. Over the weekend, Herbert Hax, one of the influential "Five Wise Men" said Bonn should put off joining the currency until its own finances were in order.

Klaus-Dieter Kuehbacher added to those worries late in the day, saying he doubted Bonn could reach its goal of cutting the deficit to 2.9 percent of gross domestic product and rejected attempts to use Maastricht Treaty leeway on EMU criteria.

Traders said that with Germany reporting somewhat stronger than expected economic data last week, it is no surprise that the spread to Treasuries has narrowed back from near 120 basis points. The spread narrowed back to 98 basis points from 101 basis points at the previous close.
A lack of German data this week should keep trading in fairly dull ranges. Two Bundesbank council members Franz-Christoph Zeitler and Helmut Hesse are to speak on Tuesday, however.
Probably the biggest event of the week does not come until Friday when U.S. producer prices are released.
